messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — the v3 API change removes the envelope wrapper and switches streaming frames. We need a compatibility wedge to avoid breaking customers. Brainstorming options.
sam: +1 we should avoid client churn. Two high-level paths: (A) a lightweight proxy/wedge that rewrites legacy envelopes to v3 shape, or (B) server-side dual-shape support for a transition window. Tradeoffs?
ben: Option A isolates complexity but adds another service in the path. latency impact could be minimized with in-process sidecar or edge lambda.
rachael: For dual support (B) we need runtime branching everywhere — adds risk and technical debt. Also harder to A/B and roll back.
maria: My instinct is wedge/proxy as a short-to-mid term plan. Can be deployed per-tenant and removed after clients migrate. Also lets us collect migration telemetry.
tim: Agree. Important to capture: request header sniffing, correct handling of streaming EOF/frame types, and KV cache keys (envelope changes affect cache keys). We should ensure cache compatibility.
sam: For streaming, wedge needs to translate old frame markers to new ones without buffering full responses — otherwise latency suffers. Pseudocode:
```
if incoming.frame == "LEGACY_CHUNK":
  forward_as("V3_CHUNK", payload)
elif incoming.frame == "LEGACY_END":
  forward_as("V3_END")
```
Make it stateless per-connection where possible.
ben: Also add a header we can use for telemetry, e.g. `X-Compat-Wedge: v1->v3` so we can measure traffic routed through wedge and success rates. And emit counters for rewrite failures.
maria: Deployment strategy proposal:
- Build wedge as small Go service + envoy filter option.
- Start with opt-in tenants behind feature flag; run for a week, collect metrics.
- Canary with 1% of traffic (non-critical clients) then 10% then broad.
- After 60 days of zero rewrite errors + client opt-ins, plan removal and client deprecation notice.
rachael: Ops concerns: wedge must have circuit-breaker and graceful degrade — if wedge fails we should 503 for opt-in only, but for default-route we should fallback to slow-mode and alert.
tim: Can we implement the wedge as an Envoy Lua filter first? Faster to iterate, lower ops burden. Longer term, a compiled sidecar if perf shows it's needed.
sam: Good idea. Lua filter will handle header rewrites and small frame mapping. For heavy throughput tenants we gate to native sidecar.
maria: Rollback plan: feature flag to opt-out any tenant, and a kill switch at infra-level. We also need migration docs and sample client patches.
ben: Action items:
- maria: draft mini-RFC + rollout runbook (owner)
- sam: prototype Envoy Lua filter (POC)
- tim: add observability spec + metrics names, SLOs
- rachael: ops runbook + circuit-breaker config
- ben: sample client diff and deprecation language
maria: I'll ship the mini-RFC today. pinging deploy-bot to create a tracking ticket.
deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-2194: "wedge proxy compatibility rollout — v3 envelope migration" assigned to maria, sam, rachael.
maria: Thanks. One more thought — we should also ensure our SDKs get a prioritized migration patch (backports for older versions) so fewer clients need wedge long-term.
rachael: Noted. We'll coordinate releases with SDK owners.
maria: Ok — looks actionable. If no objections we'll proceed with the wedge-first plan. :thumbsup:
